title: Team config
description: The ONLY per-team file. Rubric, taxonomy and output format are shared and must not be copied here.

default.description: Use this team when no --team is given and the tickets' project key does not decide it. A default in the user's folder outranks the plugin's shipped one.

members.description: Who belongs to this team, for choosing a team when no ticket names one (the queue, the doctor). Exact addresses, or a whole domain written '*@example.com'. An exact address outranks a domain. Matched locally only; never sent anywhere.

instance_id.description: Tracker instance identifier (Atlassian calls this the cloud id).

priority_names.description: Maps P1-P4 to this project's priority field values.

voc_destination.description: Where voice-of-customer items are routed. Project key, board, or 'none'.

component_label_prefix.description: For trackers with no component field: the label prefix that marks a component, e.g. 'component-' for 'component-approvals'. Used to scope history and duplicates and to show the area in the queue.

tracker.description: Issue tracker. Field names are tracker-neutral; the shipped adapter targets Atlassian by default.

sources.description: Per-source mode. 'live' calls MCP, 'fixture' reads a recorded response, 'off' skips.

datasource_uid.description: metrics: the log or metrics store's data source id, e.g. a Grafana data source uid.

queries.description: metrics: read-only query templates by purpose (error_rate, deploys, expected_heartbeat). Placeholders like <area-service> and <error text from the ticket> are filled in per ticket.

deploys.description: metrics: a hosting platform that records deploys and runtime logs, used with tool_bindings.metrics.deploy_events and runtime_logs.

provider.description: Display name of the system behind this source (for example the tracker or log store product), shown in reports next to the source name. Set by triage-config from the connector it bound.

manifest_sources.description: Ordered list of release-manifest adapters. First that returns data wins per field; later ones enrich. Align with the org's ecosystem.

title_pattern.description: Regex capturing the version from the page title, e.g. 'Release (?<version>\\d{4}\\.\\d{2})'.

wiki.description: Wiki release-note pages. Keys match wiki but any wiki with labelled pages fits.

vcs.description: Version control. Only these adapters yield file-level detail.

manual_file_path.description: Required when manual_file is in manifest_sources. A path to a releases envelope; a relative path resolves beside the team config first, then inside the plugin.

warehouse.description: Analytics warehouse. All product-specific SQL lives here, never in a shared skill.

default_branch.description: Branch a fix should start from, written into the fix brief. Defaults to 'main' when unset.

owner.description: Organisation or user that owns the repository on the code host. Needed for file reads.

tool_bindings.description: Per-source MCP tool-name suffixes. Required for every source in live mode, the tracker included. This plugin declares no MCP servers of its own: it binds to whatever tools are already in the session, from an account connector, another plugin, or a local server. Tool names differ between deployments, which is why they are configuration.

output.description: Where the triage report is written and whether to write one.

reports_dir.description: Relative to the working directory, not the plugin. The plugin may be installed in a temporary location.

report_format.description: Which report files a triage writes. 'html' (default) writes only <TICKET>-report.html, the full report with the run trace. 'md' writes only <TICKET>.md. 'both' writes both. 'agent' writes no report for people: only the result file and, for defects, the fix brief, for a pipeline that hands defects to a fix agent. A user can ask for another format in a single run without changing this. The fix brief is written for every defect in every mode.

theme.description: Accent colour for the HTML pages (report, queue, batch). Everything else about the look is in assets/report-theme.css.

accent_dark.description: Dark mode accent; defaults to accent.

run_trace.description: Where the HTML report (which carries the run trace) goes. 'file' writes <TICKET>-report.html in reports_dir. 'never' writes no HTML, so the report falls back to markdown. 'artifact' publishes a hosted page, where the client can. Default is 'file' because a trace carries customer names and account counts, so publishing is opt-in per team rather than automatic.

links.description: URL templates for evidence links, used only when a tool returns no URL. Renderers show a short label with the URL behind it, never a bare URL. Placeholders: code {owner} {repo} {ref} {path} {line}; commit {owner} {repo} {sha}; release {owner} {repo} {version}; pr {owner} {repo} {number}; ticket {key}.

log_query.description: Opens a metrics or log query in the metrics tool. Placeholders {query} (filled JSON-escaped and URL-encoded) {from} {to} (epoch ms). Rebuilds every result link that carries a `query`, even one a tool returned, because deep-link tools can emit an older URL shape that opens an empty query.

queue.description: How long a bug may wait for triage before the queue flags it overdue and puts it first. Unset keys use the defaults.

at_risk.description: Hours for a ticket carrying an at-risk label.

by_priority.description: Hours by the tracker's own priority value, e.g. {"Critical": 8}. The shortest applicable limit wins.

stuck_after_days.description: A ticket triaged as P1 or P2 with no tracker activity for this many days is flagged as stuck.

automation.description: Automatic triage. Off by default. When on, a scheduler or a tracker event runs triage-auto, which triages new and changed bugs unattended and writes a review digest. It never writes to the tracker.

trigger.description: schedule: a scheduled task runs it. event: a tracker webhook or CI job runs it with the new ticket keys.

lookback_hours.description: Only bugs created within this window are picked up, plus any that are overdue.

retriage_changed.description: Re-triage a ticket updated since its last triage.

tracker_write.description: Automatic triage never writes to the tracker. Reserved so that a future opt-in is explicit.

verification.description: Checking that a workaround works before the report recommends it. Off by default. The runner decides where the check runs. Never production.

runner.description: http: a hosted preview or staging deployment. docker: a local container started and stopped by the commands below. ci: a workflow dispatched through tool_bindings.verification. command: a test command the team wrote.

environment.description: Where the runner points. production is refused.

headers_from_env.description: Header name to the NAME of an environment variable holding its value. Values are never written here.

run.description: {scenario} is replaced by the scenario file path. Exit 0 means the workaround works.

calibration.description: When the accuracy review suggests a rubric or config change.

min_overrides.description: Overrides of the same kind needed before a suggestion is made.

min_rate.description: Share of reviewed runs that must disagree the same way.

comments.description: How the triaged ticket's own comment thread is filtered before the model reads it. Bots, chasers, status echoes, repeats and quoted email tails are dropped by script; the rest is read and each comment used is quoted.

bot_authors.description: Author names that are automation in this tracker, in addition to names matching bot, automation, CI or noreply.

staff.description: Addresses or '*@domain' of staff, whose comments are always kept. Used only when the tracker does not say who is staff.

max_kept.description: Most comments passed to the model after filtering; the newest are kept.

risks.description: Named risk types for defects (scripts/risks.py). Risks name the kind of harm; they never change the priority by themselves.

terms.description: Extra words per risk type, for this team's domain. Keys: security, payment, data_integrity, compliance, availability, silent_failure, customer_communication, performance.

off.description: Risk types this team does not want tagged.

human_review.description: Hold defects that carry chosen risks (scripts/risks.py) for a person's decision. Off by default.

min_level.description: How sure a risk must be to trigger the gate.

reviewers.description: Who may confirm, by name or '*@domain'. Empty means any person.

sla.description: Fix-by dates per priority (scripts/sla.py). Off unless fix_within is set. Never changes the priority.
